walkthroughs.body_html:
Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis — a core area of English Literature.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Paper 1: Guided Literary Analysis.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Who coined the term ostranenie (defamiliarisation) in 1917?
options: Viktor Shklovsky
Roman Jakobson
Boris Eikhenbaum
Yuri Tynyanov

mcqs.q: Whose 1946 essay attacked the intentional fallacy?
options: Wimsatt and Beardsley
Brooks and Warren
Frye and Bloom
Empson and Richards

mcqs.q: What is the structure of a Shakespearean sonnet?
options: A sonnet is any short love poem.
Fourteen lines in iambic pentameter, structured as three quatrains and a final couplet, rhyming ABAB CDCD EFEF GG, often with a volta near the couplet.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.

mcqs.q: What defines epic poetry as a genre?
options: A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
Long narrative poems on heroic subjects, in elevated style, often invoking a muse, in medias res openings, and treating events of national or cosmic significance.
Epic means any story with a battle in it.
Epic means any poem that is very long.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.
A line of five iambs (unstressed-stressed syllable pairs), creating a ten-syllable line with the rhythm da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM.
Iambic pentameter is any line with ten syllables.
A sonnet must always be exactly ten lines long.
